title: Rome's next reason: heretics of every age rejected traditions — so contempt marks heresy
source_text: XXII. Sed praeter Scripturae sacrae testimonia, quibus Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae traditionis non scriptae authoritatem fulcire annituntur, in eundem finem proferunt argumenta quaedam ex ratione ducta. Et primo quidem argumentum ducunt ex consensu haereticorum in traditionibus contemnendis. Nam, inquiunt, haeretici omnium aetatum traditiones rejecerunt. Ideoque traditionum contemptus, & rejectio est veluti haereseos nota & indicium. Quod autem haeretici traditiones semper rejecerint, probant per inductionem & exemplum Valentinianorum, Marcionitarum, Donatistarum, Arianorum, Eunomianorum, Nestorii, Eutychetis, Aerianorum, & aliorum quorundam.
pass_a_gloss: But besides the testimonies of sacred Scripture by which the Doctors of the Roman Church strive to prop up the authority of unwritten tradition, they bring forward for the same end certain arguments drawn from reason. And first indeed they draw an argument from the consent of heretics in despising traditions. For, they say, heretics of all ages have rejected traditions. And therefore contempt and rejection of traditions is as it were a mark and indication of heresy. But that heretics have always rejected traditions they prove by induction and the example of the Valentinians, Marcionites, Donatists, Arians, Eunomians, Nestorius, Eutyches, Aerians, and certain others.
pass_b_english: Beyond the texts, Rome argues from reason.
First: heretics in every age despised traditions.
So rejecting tradition is treated as a heresy-mark.
They list Valentinians, Marcionites, Donatists, Arians, Eunomians, Nestorius, Eutyches, Aerians, and more.
